title: Rubio’s visits are not enough to reset India–US relations
gist: Chietigj Bajpaee argues India-US ties remain structurally 'sticky' (about US$240bn trade in 2025, deep military and tech ties) but Trump's flip-flopping on India's Russian oil purchases, 50% tariffs and sanctions threats has done lasting damage. Rubio's Mumbai and Jamnagar visit centred on energy, including India's role as second-largest buyer of Venezuelan heavy crude after Maduro's capture; a trade deal and a Manila Quad summit are the key watchpoints.

insights.claim: Despite a year of tariffs, sanctions and visa tightening, India-US structural engagement remains strong, with bilateral goods and services trade around US$240 billion in 2025.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Commercial ties are resilient to political noise.
insights.quote: Bilateral trade in goods and services grew to around US$240 billion in 2025.

insights.claim: India conducts more joint military exercises with the US than any other country, and tech cooperation includes a 2025 joint satellite and massive pledged US tech AI investment in India.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Supports continued US tech and AI capex in India.

insights.claim: Rubio skipping New Delhi is not a sign of decline, as Xi, Starmer and Merz also bypassed the capital on recent visits.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee

themes.theme: Energy at the core of Rubio's trip

insights.claim: Rubio visited Jamnagar, home to Reliance Industries' world's largest refinery, amid oil price pressure from the US-Israel war with Iran.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Reliance is central to US-India energy diplomacy.

insights.claim: India became the second-largest buyer of Venezuelan heavy crude, mostly processed at Jamnagar, after the US captured Nicolás Maduro in January.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Reliance benefits from discounted Venezuelan heavy crude flows.

insights.claim: Trump announced in March that Reliance will invest in a major refinery in Brownsville, Texas.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Reliance US refining capex is a bilateral deal sweetener.

insights.claim: Trump's flip-flopping on India's purchase of Russian crude, including 50% tariffs and threatened secondary sanctions, has done lasting damage to the relationship.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Policy volatility raises risk premia on India-US trade-exposed sectors.
insights.quote: the US flip-flopping on India’s purchase of Russian crude has been nothing short of staggering

insights.claim: In February 2026 the US cut tariffs on India under an interim trade-deal framework in exchange for suspending Russian oil purchases, then partly reversed by allowing purchases of Russian oil stranded at sea after Strait of Hormuz disruptions.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Russian-crude access for Indian refiners swings with US policy.

insights.claim: The September 2026 Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act authorised tariffs up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas including India, but Trump waived penalties in October with a 60-day review to follow.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: 60-day review is a near-term tariff-risk catalyst for India.

insights.claim: Trump waived Russian-oil penalties partly because the US is now buying Russian diesel itself, prioritising curbing inflation before the midterms over long-term strategy.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: US energy-sanctions enforcement is subordinated to domestic inflation politics.

insights.claim: Peter Navarro labelled India a 'laundromat for the Kremlin'.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Illustrates hostile rhetoric within the administration.

insights.claim: Two pillars of India-US ties, shared democratic values and India as a China counterbalance, have weakened as both independently seek to reset relations with Beijing.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: India's China-hedge premium for US policy is diminishing.
insights.quote: Two key pillars of the India–US relationship have weakened under Trump: the countries’ shared democratic values and India’s role as a counterbalance to China.

insights.claim: Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau said the US would not repeat the 'mistake' made with China by letting India become an economic competitor.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Signals US may resist India's manufacturing rise, a risk to 'China+1' India thesis.

insights.claim: A long-delayed bilateral trade agreement and a Quad leaders' summit planned in Manila in November are key watchpoints for a structural shift, though India's finance minister says talks have hit a 'plateau'.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Trade deal signing would cut tariff risk on Indian exporters.

insights.claim: A lasting reset requires rediscovering the strategic rationale of the relationship rather than platitudes or episodic dealmaking.
insights.speaker: Chietigj Bajpaee
insights.so_what: Expect continued transactional volatility absent strategic realignment.
